recommendation: Keep this focused source correction. It preserves the MnM-approved flexible base ContactPoint behavior while accurately documenting the optional machine-friendly TEL URI extension.
issue_request: FHIR-5200 was a Published/Persuasive MnM ballot issue asking whether ContactPoint phone/fax values should be RFC 3966 tel URIs. The final resolution kept base ContactPoint.value flexible for human-entered numbers and promised a standard extension for a machine-friendly URI form when needed.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn revision 4532, mirrored as git commit de9700d3959339348e2f321ebe752a066f12cf28, which added the ISO 21090 profile spreadsheet and a ContactPoint example. The current example descended from that application and still linked to rfc3966.txt while labeling the syntax as RFC 3166.
additional_context: The current ContactPoint base text still explains that phone/fax values are not formal URLs because legacy and clerical practices often prevent strict formatting. The iso21090-TEL-address definition now lives in the FHIR Extension Pack as an active ContactPoint extension with an RFC 3966 conformant url value. FHIR-27754 later corrected the same example's value type to valueUrl and is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Updated source/datatypes-examples.html to change the stale RFC 3166 label to RFC 3966 in the ContactPoint ISO 21090 TEL example. No core extension-definition edit was needed because the extension-pack definition is already correct.
source_changes: source/datatypes-examples.html: changed the ContactPoint ISO 21090 TEL example prose from RFC 3166 to RFC 3966.

related_jiras.note: A later Published/Persuasive correction to the same ContactPoint iso21090-TEL-address example fixed valueUrl; it is already represented on the combined branch and was not decided again.
